descriptor: CNC machine-tool maker with a French subsidiary
lede: Rajkot-based Jyoti CNC makes CNC machines from entry-level to 5-axis, with the French maker Huron as a subsidiary. Profit swung from losses to a 16-17% net margin in three years as defence and auto orders (order book ₹5,082 Cr) arrived, but half of FY27 revenue is still to come in H2 and the 25% margin promise is not yet met.

short_version.text: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue +31% at a 28% EBITDA margin, a record 1,911 machines dispatched, order book ₹5,082 Cr, and a ₹255 Cr central subsidy approved for in-house controllers and motors.

Consolidated margin is about 22% against the 25% promised, Huron revenue has not ramped, an unresolved French investigation hangs over Huron, and operating cash flow was negative in FY24 and FY25 with inventory above 450 days.
75x earnings and 45x EBITDA already assume the H2 ramp and the controller strategy work.

blocks.text: Jyoti CNC designs, casts, machines and assembles CNC machines in Rajkot and sells through 15,000+ customers across automotive, aerospace and defence, general engineering and electronics. Its French subsidiary Huron makes large machines for defence and aerospace customers. About 60% of India's CNC demand is imported, so domestic makers are gaining share.

items.text: Q2 revenue: automotive 36%, general engineering 28%, aerospace and defence 21%, electronics 7%. Order book is 36% aerospace and defence.
Moving from a mechanical company toward mechatronics (own controllers, motors, drives) and later robotics; ECMS subsidy of 25% on ₹1,020 Cr over five years.

blocks.title: Net profit vs operating cash flow, ₹ Cr
blocks.caption: Five-year profit of ₹750 Cr against operating cash flow of only −₹18 Cr.

items.text: Profit has not turned into cash: inventory days of 378-469 and a 359-day cash cycle absorb it. H1 FY27 operating cash flow was reported at about ₹112 Cr, the first strong half.
Debt rose from ₹304 Cr (FY24) to ₹946 Cr (Sep 2026) to fund capacity; borrowings/equity 0.44x.
ROIIC over FY24-FY26 about 17% (additional capital employed ₹1,186 Cr).

cells.text: In use; foundry only starting Q3

blocks.text: The MD repeats the same targets each call and was candid when asked about Huron's export licences and the French probe, but several lines (H2 about 60% of the year, 25% margin) rest on a back-loaded second half.

items.text: Promoters 62.55%, FIIs 5.3% (down from 9.9% a year ago), DIIs 12.9%; no pledge shown on Screener.

French authorities opened an investigation into Huron in April 2026 (status quo since); aerospace and defence order intake dipped in Q2 on delayed tenders; annual-report checks (auditor, related-party dealings) were not made for this note.

cells: About 60% of Indian demand is imported

items.text: Vertically integrated casting and machining, a 40,000-machine installed base and a customer base where management says one-third are 'die-hard'.
Controller and spindle supply from Japan and Europe is tight; the controller project has no revenue yet and global peers have struggled to build accepted controllers.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our own assumptions, not a forecast or advice.

Jyoti CNC has the order book and the subsidy to support its growth story, but at 75x earnings the stock already pays for a smooth H2 and for success in controllers. The base case assumes growth near the guided 25-30% and a margin that settles near 14% net; the evidence of H1 (about 22% EBITDA margin, thin cash flow) does not yet prove it.
